strings.d1.s0.name: Castle Square Sigismund's Column
strings.d1.s0.tips: A UNESCO-listed old town flattened in 1944 and rebuilt brick by brick; see the king's column.
strings.d1.s1.name: Royal Castle Warsaw
strings.d1.s1.tips: The royal castle, with Rembrandts and Canaletto's views of Warsaw (used in the reconstruction). Free on Wednesdays.
strings.d1.s2.name: Old Town Market Square Syrenka
strings.d1.s2.tips: The mermaid statue, colourful merchants' houses, the Barbican and the city walls.
strings.d1.s3.name: Zapiecek Pierogarnia
strings.d1.s3.tips: A pierogi chain (in the old town): try ruskie and fried pierogi, with kompot (fruit drink).
strings.d1.s4.name: Krakowskie Przedmieście
strings.d1.s4.tips: The Royal Route: the Presidential Palace, Chopin benches (they play music), the University and the Bristol hotel.
strings.d1.b0.name: Bar Mleczny Pod Barbakanem
strings.d1.b0.tips: A milk bar in the old town: kotlet (breaded cutlet) and naleśniki (filled crêpes).
strings.d1.b1.name: Warsaw Uprising Monument & Krasiński Garden
strings.d1.b1.tips: The uprising monument and park, as an alternative to the tower.
strings.d2.s0.name: POLIN Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: 1,000 years of Polish Jewish history in one of Europe's best museums, with a wooden synagogue ceiling. Free on Thursdays, closed Tuesdays.
strings.d2.s1.name: Ghetto Heroes Monument
strings.d2.s1.tips: Rapoport's monument in front of the museum, where Willy Brandt knelt.
strings.d2.s2.name: Charlotte Menora Plac Grzybowski
strings.d2.s2.tips: A bakery-café next to the Nożyk Synagogue: bread and chałka (braided bread).
strings.d2.s3.name: Nożyk Synagogue
strings.d2.s3.tips: The only synagogue to survive the war; Próżna Street has surviving ghetto houses.
strings.d2.s4.name: Hala Koszyki
strings.d2.s4.tips: A 1908 market hall turned food hall; come in the evening.
strings.d2.b0.name: Jewish Historical Institute
strings.d2.b0.tips: The Ringelblum Archive; an alternative to the synagogue.
strings.d2.b1.name: Bar Bambino Mleczny
strings.d2.b1.tips: A milk bar on Krucza Street.
strings.d3.s0.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
strings.d3.s0.tips: The 1944 uprising: the 3D film 'City of Ruins' and a sewer tunnel. Closed Tuesdays, free on Thursdays, book online.
strings.d3.s1.name: Wola Murals Elektrownia Powiśle
strings.d3.s1.tips: A shopping and dining complex in an old power station, on the Vistula bank.
strings.d3.s2.name: Elektrownia Powiśle Food Hall
strings.d3.s3.name: Copernicus Science Centre
strings.d3.s3.tips: Interactive science, good with children, with a planetarium and a riverside setting.
strings.d3.s4.name: Vistula Boulevards
strings.d3.s4.tips: A winter riverside walk, with the Copernicus Science Centre's roof nearby.
strings.d3.b0.name: Neon Museum Soho Factory
strings.d3.b0.tips: Communist-era neon signs in Praga, as an alternative to the science centre.
strings.d3.b1.name: Bar Prasowy Mleczny
strings.d3.b1.tips: A legendary milk bar on Marszałkowska Street.
strings.d4.s0.name: Łazienki Park
strings.d4.s0.tips: The royal park, with peacocks and the Chopin monument (free concerts on summer Sundays at 12:00 and 16:00).
strings.d4.s1.name: Palace on the Isle
strings.d4.s1.tips: A neoclassical summer palace on an island, built for Poniatowski.
strings.d4.s2.name: Belvedere Restaurant Łazienki
strings.d4.s2.tips: A smart lunch in the orangery; a park café is the alternative.
strings.d4.s3.name: Wilanów Palace
strings.d4.s3.tips: Poland's Versailles (King Sobieski), with a baroque garden. Take bus 116 or 180; in winter there is a garden of lights.
strings.d4.s4.name: Wilanów Poster Museum
strings.d4.s4.tips: The Polish poster school, next to the palace.
strings.d4.b0.name: Łazienki Amphitheatre Café
strings.d4.b0.tips: A café inside the park for a light bite.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ujazdów Castle CSW
strings.d4.b1.tips: A contemporary art centre next to Łazienki, as an alternative to Wilanów.
strings.d5.s0.name: Ząbkowska Street Praga
strings.d5.s0.tips: The right bank, which survived the war: brick courtyards, shrines to the Virgin Mary and street art. 10 minutes by tram.
strings.d5.s1.name: Koneser Polish Vodka Museum
strings.d5.s1.tips: A museum in an old vodka factory with 3 tastings, in the Koneser courtyard.
strings.d5.s2.name: Różycki Bazaar
strings.d5.s2.tips: An open-air market from 1901; pyzy (potato dumplings) come straight from the jar.
strings.d5.s3.name: Bar Mleczny Rusałka Praga
strings.d5.s3.tips: An unchanged retro milk bar next to Praga Park.
strings.d5.s4.name: Soho Factory & Neon Museum
strings.d5.s4.tips: A factory complex with a neon museum and cafés.
strings.d5.b0.name: W Oparach Absurdu
strings.d5.b0.tips: A bar with absurdist décor on Ząbkowska Street; try the vodka.
strings.d5.b1.name: Warsaw Zoo
strings.d5.b1.tips: The zoo from The Zookeeper's Wife, in Praga, as an alternative to Soho.
strings.d6.s0.name: Palace of Culture and Science
strings.d6.s0.tips: Stalin's 237 m gift: a terrace on the 30th floor with a city panorama.
strings.d6.s1.name: Fryderyk Chopin Museum
strings.d6.s1.tips: Multimedia exhibits in the Ostrogski Palace, including his last piano. Free on Sundays.
strings.d6.s2.name: Kafka Powiśle
strings.d6.s2.tips: A bohemian café next to the Chopin Museum, overlooking the river.
strings.d6.s3.name: Holy Cross Church Chopin's Heart
strings.d6.s3.tips: Chopin's heart is in a pillar, on Krakowskie Przedmieście.
strings.d6.s4.name: Chopin Concert Chopin Point
strings.d6.s4.tips: An evening Chopin recital in the old town (daily); in summer, free Sunday concerts in Łazienki.
strings.d6.b0.name: Restauracja Zoni Koneser
strings.d6.b0.tips: Modern Polish cuisine in Praga, as an alternative to the concert.
strings.d6.b1.name: National Museum Warsaw
strings.d6.b1.tips: Matejko's Grunwald, as an alternative to the Chopin Museum. Free on Tuesdays.
strings.d7.s0.name: Saska Kępa Francuska Street
strings.d7.s0.tips: Modernist villas and cafés in a quiet right-bank neighbourhood.
strings.d7.s1.name: Skwer Breakfast Saska Kępa
strings.d7.s1.tips: A neighbourhood café for a farewell breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: Stadion Narodowy from outside
strings.d7.s2.tips: The red-and-white national stadium, across the Vistula.
strings.d7.s3.name: Warszawa Centralna Airport Train
strings.d7.s3.tips: The train to Chopin Airport takes 20 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Cafe Kulturalna Palace of Culture
strings.d7.b0.tips: A café inside the palace, as an alternative to Saska Kępa.
strings.d7.b1.name: Muzeum Historii Polski Cytadela
strings.d7.b1.tips: A huge new history museum, opened in 2023, in the citadel.
strings.note0: Tram, metro and bus tickets: 20 minutes cost 3.40 PLN, a day pass 15 PLN. Use the Jakdojade app. The SKM airport train takes 20 minutes. The city is spread out, so you will need the tram.
strings.note1: Winter is -3 to 3°C with snow. In December the Christmas market is in the old town and the garden of lights is at Wilanów; museums are quiet and milk bars are warm.
strings.note2: Pierogi cost 30-40 PLN, a milk bar meal 20 PLN, the vodka museum 60 PLN, POLIN 45 PLN and the Uprising Museum 30 PLN. Poland is good value, cards are accepted everywhere and the tip is 10%.
strings.note3: Free days at museums: Royal Castle on Wednesday, POLIN on Thursday, Uprising Museum on Thursday, National Museum on Tuesday. POLIN and the Uprising Museum are CLOSED on Tuesday.
strings.note4: Milk bar (bar mleczny): take a tray, order at the counter, then pay at the till. Try Prasowy, Bambino or Rusałka.
strings.note5: Try Żubrówka with apple juice, żurek (sour rye soup), bigos (hunter's stew) and pączki (doughnuts; Fat Thursday falls on a Thursday).
